newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA RUPEE ENDS FIRM DESPITE RBI DOLLAR PURCHASES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA RUPEE ENDS FIRM DESPITE RBI DOLLAR PURCHASES.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Monday stronger at 35.700/705 per dollar after opening quotes at 35.715/725 on good supply of the U.S. currency, dealers said.
"It was a day of (dollar) sellers," said a dealer at a European bank. "The market was flush with dollars and accumulated weekend remittances added to the supply."
Dealers said most of the early trades were at 35.71/72 levels and the rupee strengthened slightly to 35.70 in the afternoon on poor demand.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened in the market around four in the evening after a leading bank quoted 35.6975/7050 rupees to a dollar, dealers said.
The RBI bought dollars at 35.71 rupees.
The rupee saw a high of 35.70 and a low of 35.72 on Monday.
The forward dollar market was volatile, with premiums opening lower, then moving up to Monday's closing levels before dipping towards close, dealer said.
"There was some paying (payment of premium for buying dollars) in April," said a dealer.
The other active months were October, January and July maturities, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium ended Monday at 4.14 percent compared with the previous 4.59 percent.
